Check Whether Package Manager Serves Binary Packages

Source: R/binary-check.R
check_binary_repos.Rd

Posit Package Manager silently serves source packages whenever it cannot match a request to a binary, for example when the repository URL is generic on an unrecognized Linux distribution or the R user agent is missing. The install then compiles every package from source.

Usage

check_binary_repos(
  repos = NULL,
  package = "cli",
  verbose = NULL,
  lockfile = NULL,
  snapshot_dates = NULL
)

Arguments

repos

Repository URLs to check. Defaults to getOption("repos"). Repositories that are not Posit Package Manager repositories, including self-hosted ones not listed in BOOSTERPAK_PPM_REPO, BOOSTERPAK_PPM_HOSTS, or options(boosterpak.ppm_hosts = c(...)), are skipped. Cannot be combined with lockfile.

package

A small package available from the repository, used as the probe. Defaults to "cli".

verbose

Whether to print routine per-repository results. Warnings are always signaled for repositories serving source, unreachable repositories, responses that cannot be interpreted, and lockfile pins that are not available as binary. The count of lockfile pins that were not compared is always reported.

lockfile

Path to an renv.lock. When given, the repositories are the ones recorded in the lockfile, and the pins are compared with their indexes as described above.

snapshot_dates

Optional dates in "YYYY-MM-DD" form, such as "2026-10-14". For each date, the pins from each Package Manager repository in lockfile are compared with that dated snapshot. Requires lockfile.

Value

A data frame with one row per checked repository, invisibly. Columns are repo, name (the repository name in repos), package, version, status (the HTTP status of the final response), package_type ("binary" or "source"), binary_tag, and binary (TRUE for binaries, FALSE for source, NA when it could not be determined).

With lockfile, the data frame also carries a "lockfile" attribute, a list with: lockfile (the path); pins (repository-sourced pins compared, M); available (N, pins available as binary); unavailable; needs_compilation (K, unavailable pins whose package needs compilation in the index); not_in_index (unavailable pins whose package is not in the index); unchecked (repository-sourced pins not compared: their repository is not a Package Manager repository, is not recorded in the lockfile, or its index could not be read); repositories (per-repository counts); offenders (one row per unavailable pin that needs compilation or is not in the index, with repository, package, pinned, current (the index version, NA when absent), available, and needs_compilation); and snapshots (counts per snapshot_dates entry, or NULL when none were given).

The "lockfile" attribute is set only when the check runs, which is on Linux. On other platforms the function returns an empty data frame without it. The attribute is present on every Linux run with lockfile, including Linux without glibc. The __linux__ rewrite described above applies only on glibc Linux.

Details

check_binary_repos() sends one HEAD request for package to each Posit Package Manager repository in repos, using the current session's HTTPUserAgent, and reports the X-Package-Type and X-Package-Binary-Tag response headers. It warns for every repository that serves source.

It also warns when download.file.method is "curl" and download.file.extra has no -L. Package Manager serves packages through a redirect that R's "curl" method does not follow on its own, so installs would save the redirect page instead of the package, even though this check passes: it uses libcurl directly and follows redirects.

The check follows the Linux binary layout, where the repository URL itself selects binaries, so it only runs on Linux; on other platforms it returns an empty data frame. It needs network access: it downloads each repository's package index with utils::available.packages() to find the current version of package, then sends the HEAD request. Nothing runs unless you call it, and nothing is installed.

Pinned versions

A project restores the versions pinned in renv.lock, not the current versions. Package Manager only serves a binary for a version that exists in the snapshot the URL points at, so a pin that is older or newer than the repository's current version can still compile from source even when the probe above passes. Pass lockfile to compare every repository-sourced pin with the index of its repository, using one index download per repository and no installs:

  • Repositories come from the lockfile's R$Repositories. Each pin is matched to one of them by its Repository field: first by repository name, then by URL with any trailing slash ignored. A value that is neither, such as RSPM, is matched to the lockfile's only Package Manager repository when there is exactly one. Pins that match no repository are not compared.

  • On glibc Linux, with boosterpak's repository setup enabled (see BOOSTERPAK_CONFIGURE_REPOSITORIES), each generic Package Manager URL is checked as the Linux binary URL a restore on this machine would use, such as <host>/cran/__linux__/manylinux_2_28/latest. Otherwise the URL as recorded is checked, because that is what a restore uses. Distro URLs such as <host>/cran/__linux__/noble/latest are checked as they are.

  • A pin is available as binary when its version equals the version in that index. Other pins, and pins missing from the index, are not available as binary. A pin that needs compilation is one whose package is marked NeedsCompilation: yes in the index. For a pin whose version differs from the index, that flag describes the current version, so it is an estimate.

  • The result is warned about when any pin is not available as binary. The worst offenders, pins that need compilation first, are listed in the warning and in the "lockfile" attribute.

  • snapshot_dates optionally compares the pins with dated snapshots that you name. Only those dates are requested. Nothing scans other dates.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
check_binary_repos()
check_binary_repos(lockfile = "renv.lock")
check_binary_repos(lockfile = "renv.lock", snapshot_dates = "2026-10-14")
} # }
